B000490.text: This week, the White House Office of Budget and Management’s Director, Russell Vought, appeared before the U.S. House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government. During the hearing, I asked the Director about how Congress can be any clearer to ensure that the Trump Administration understands that once a funding bill is signed into law, the President is not allowed to change or second-guess the spending and withhold it due to policy or political differences. That is at the heart of Article 1 of the U.S. Constitution and why Congress also passed the Impoundment Control Act of 1974, when President Nixon tried to withhold funds that were already obligated according to the law.

This week, I asked the White House Office of Budget and Management’s Director, Russell Vought, to explain how poorly planned cuts to the federal workforce last year have weakened services and protections upon which Americans rely. This includes the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service, which is responsible for protecting America’s agriculture from invasive species and diseases. USDA-APHIS began mounting a vigorous response to the resurgence of New World Screwworm – a deadly parasite affecting livestock – in 2024. However, in early 2025, the Administration illegally fired workers and forced others to resign, causing over 25 percent of all USDA-APHIS employees to leave. USDA’s New World Screwworm prevention, monitoring, surveillance, and control efforts were halted. USDA had approved $378 million in prevention and control funding for sterile fly facilities in 2023 and 2024, yet the money went unspent when the new administration paused funding. This is extremely concerning to our ranchers, and this outbreak could drive the price of food even higher. Unfortunately, we continue to see the fallout of the blunt and ill-considered cuts to federal workers, from the return of New World Screwworm to the United States, to farmers showing up to closed or understaffed Farm Service Agency offices, to attacks on our nuclear safety programs putting national security at risk. I will continue to hold the White House accountable, as I did this week during the U.S. House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government hearing with Mr. Vought.

The law created the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, which has returned billions of dollars to Americans who were cheated by scams, junk fees, and predatory lenders. Recognizing Hiram Bingham IV with a permanent day of remembrance is a fitting tribute to a U.S. diplomat and a Connecticut resident whose story is one of the finest examples of American courage. Last week, I joined the Bingham family for the inaugural Hiram Bingham IV Day in Connecticut. As vice-consul in the visa section of the American consulate in Marseille, Hiram Bingham IV risked his career to help thousands of predominantly Jewish refugees escape Nazi persecution. His courage saved thousands of lives during one of history’s darkest chapters. It was especially meaningful to hear from members of Hiram Bingham’s family, including his son David Bingham, and from descendants of those whose lives changed by his actions. Today, Hiram Bingham’s legacy is more important than ever as millions of displaced people around the world are seeking safety and refugee admissions in the U.S. have fallen to historic lows. Thank you to Southern CT State Professor Dr. David Pettigrew and everyone who worked to establish this annual day of recognition for a man who deserves a permanent place in our state’s history, and now has one.

For 250 years, our great experiment has faltered, flourished, evolved, and progressed. The American experience is ever-changing and as diverse as the people who call this country home. But one thing has remained constant – the idea of America has always been a beacon of hope. Protecting this country and the ideals and values it was founded on takes work. Democracy is demanding. It takes dedication and principle. And it takes the resounding belief that upholding those ideals and values is worth the fight because America is bigger than any one person. Because liberty can only truly endure when it is paired with responsibility, virtue, and a commitment to put public good ahead of personal ambition. Today, we celebrate the moment when our founding fathers openly declared that creating this country, based in liberty, was a necessity in the face of tyranny. Their legacy is that leadership requires courage when it’s difficult, integrity when no one is watching, and a willingness to put country above self. We must remember that our duty is not merely to the next election, but to the next generation. That should be the challenge for all Americans as we look forward to another 250 years. From Massachusetts, where the fight for freedom first began, I wish you a happy 4th of July. God Bless America always, God Bless all who call her home, and God Bless our courageous men and women in uniform who continue the fight for liberty today.

On Monday, our office suffered an unimaginable loss. Chris Matthews, my District Outreach and Communications Director, passed away unexpectedly. If any one of you begin to lose faith in our country, remember Chris Matthews. Remember he was without question one of the Commonwealth’s sharpest political minds – a generational talent. Remember that he was more than a Congressional aide. He took the belief that through our actions we all can bring needed change and brought it with him on many interstate bus rides to canvas distant pivotal states and to the doors of the families he inspired. Remember through his example that public service is a genuinely noble vocation. As a trusted member of our office, he helped countless veterans, families, and those who could not advocate for themselves. Those of us privileged to have worked with him for over fifteen years will remember his laugh and his wry, often biting, humor – contrasting the way things are to the way they could be. We will always remember his authentic belief that in this country, people can bring about progress and meaningful change. It was real to him and his sincerity shown through. Chris was a genuinely good person. He was family to all of us, and we are devastated by his loss, particularly at such a young age. Our thoughts and prayers are with Molly and Eli and the many who loved him. Though we wish we had more time with him, his memory will continue to give us faith that one person can significantly make better the lives of those around him.

L000582.text: RT by @RepTedLieu: BREAKING: RIGHTEOUS FURY! Rep. Ted Lieu humiliates Trump's UN Ambassador for getting "fired" from his last job during an explosive hearing — and Waltz absolutely loses it. This is EXACTLY how you trigger a thin-skinned MAGA goon... "American service members are in the Middle East risking their lives in the war with Iran," said Lieu. "How many U.S. troops have been wounded in the Iran War?" "My understanding from the Defense Department's latest numbers is over 100, but about 70% or 90% of those have immediately returned to duty," replied Ambassador Mike Waltz. "Okay, that number is wrong," Lieu said bluntly. "According to the Defense Calculated Analysis System, 482 American troops have been wounded. Now, it's not surprising to me that you did not know the answer to that. The reason you are here today and in your position is because you were fired by the president from your former position as National Security Advisor—" "The President has never said a negative word about me—" raged back Waltz. "You disclosed classified information that harmed American pilots and put them at risk!" said Lieu. "That's your spin, I guess, for your next campaign commercial. I don't know," said Waltz. There was no "spin" involved in the congressman's assessment. Waltz was removed as National Security Advisor after the infamous SignalGate incident in which he accidentally added the editor of The Atlantic to a group chat where administration officials were discussing strikes on the Houthis in Yemen. It was a stunning security breach that could have easily resulted in dead Americans had he added someone connected to foreign intelligence. The man is an incompetent buffoon who was given the U.N. Ambassadorship because he's fanatically loyal to Trump. "How many American troops have been killed in the Iran War?" Lieu continued. "In these ongoing operations, 18," said Waltz. "Okay. Now, President Trump has repeatedly stated that Iran's military was obliterated. On March 16th, President Trump stated that Iran's military was, quote, literally obliterated, end quote," said Lieu. "How is it possible that 482 American troops have been wounded and 18 service members killed by an Iranian military that's been purportedly obliterated?" "The Iranian Navy, Air Force, air defense system, and industrial capacity have been massively damaged if not completely ineffective," said Waltz. "But this is a state that is trying to reconstitute." Boasting about destroying the Iranian Navy and Air Force is a bit like boasting that you destroyed their catapults, horse-mounted cavalry, and triremes. Their ships were incredibly outdated, as were their obsolete Cold War era jets. Destroying them accomplished nothing. Their military force projection capabilities always rested in their drone and ballistic missile programs, which continue to devastate American bases in the region. "This is a state, a regime that is obsessed with a nuclear weapon," lied Waltz. "And it's a regime that still maintains some missile and drone capability that it's firing on all of its neighbors, including our bases. I think that's a pretty common sense evaluation. But if I need to explain it to you further, I can." "You need to explain to American people how an Iranian military that's been purportedly obliterated killed 18 U.S. service members and wounded 482 service members!" said Lieu. "As you know, seven of those service members died in a plane crash—" claimed Waltz. "Let me finish my question!" said Lieu. "And has struck multiple U.S. facilities in the Middle East repeatedly. So I'm going to show you a video from Jordan. And this is an Iranian strike..." The congressman then played a video of a massive military explosion. For some suspicious reason, the audio was removed, likely because Republicans knew that the bombastic audio of the attack would make it even more terrifying — and thus drive home the fact that this war is a disaster for the United States. "Thank you. I would hope the Republican-controlled Foreign Affairs Committee would know how to use audio next time," said Lieu. "But we did see the video and it showed multiple missiles hitting this base in Jordan. Let me tell you what happened. It was disclosed later that two U.S. troops died in that strike from a purportedly obliterated Iranian military." "And this is what Donald Trump said..." Lieu went on. "He said that the Iranians, quote, did slip something through in Jordan. And if we had other operators, it would not have happened." "He then went on to say, 'When you let other people do your job — with the United States, we let other people do a job — and sometimes it doesn't work out so well.' So let me ask you this question. Do we still have American troops stationed in Jordan right now?" asked Lieu. "Doesn't surprise me that you're referring to Al Jazeera. In terms of your video..." said Waltz, desperate to change the subject and distract. "I'm here as the U.N. Ambassador, but I'm happy to refer you to Pete Hegseth, Secretary Hegseth's testimony yesterday. Of course, we still have troops in Jordan." "In your opening statement, you bragged about doing a Security Council resolution on Iran!" thundered Lieu, his voice infused with appropriate anger. "So yes, Iran is in your job responsibility! Focus on it and focus on the troops that have been wounded and killed." "Do not be so callous with the safety and lives of American troops!" he went on. "I'm going to ask you again, are U.S. troops currently stationed in Jordan?" "Try to get reelected," Waltz shot back weakly. "I will," Lieu said. "November is coming for you and this administration. Are U.S. troops stationed in Jordan? It's not even a trick question. Are they?" "Of course they are," said Waltz. "Okay, and if Donald Trump doesn't trust the Jordanians to protect U.S. troops? You trust them?" asked Lieu. "Who are we going to have protect U.S. troops? They are exposed right now in the Middle East. Repeatedly being exposed to Iranian missiles, missiles, strikes and drones." "I didn't hear this from you when they died during the Biden administration!" whined Waltz. The difference, of course, is that under President Biden the United States didn't start any new wars. In fact, Biden had the courage to finally end the Afghanistan War despite a steep political cost to his White House. He was concerned with America's national security and interests. Trump is concerned with doing Benjamin Netanyahu's bidding. "You don't even know how many U.S. troops were wounded in this Iran War!" roared Lieu. "Shame on you for not even knowing basic facts. You are the U.S. Ambassador and you don't even know how many U.S. troops were wounded in the Iran war. You got that wrong! You should be shameful! You don't know basic facts. You should resign! You don't even care about the number of U.S. troops that were wounded! You did not know how many U.S. troops were wounded! You gave false information to Congress!" "This is ridiculous!" complained Waltz, visibly upset. "You should be ashamed of yourself for not even knowing how many U.S. troops were wounded in the Iranian war," the congressman concluded. This is how EVERY member of Congress should sound when questioning these MAGA hatchet men. This Iran War has forever destroyed the myth that Republicans "support our troops." The Trump White House is treating our brave soldiers like disposable pawns to be sacrificed for no clear goals, all in the service of Israel's national interests and the profits of the military-industrial complex. Ted Lieu is right. They should be ashamed. Please ❤️ and share to thank Ted Lieu!

B001295.text: Peace through strength isn’t just a slogan. It means having the factories, shipyards, and supply chains to build what our military needs, and never depending on our adversaries for it. Today I voted for the National Defense Authorization Act to bring defense production back home, strengthen our deterrence against China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea, and give our service members a well-earned pay raise along with better housing and childcare for the families who serve right alongside them. There’s nothing more America First than that.

Taxpayers have a right to know where their hard-earned money is going. But right now billions in federal spending flows through special agreements that never show up on the public books. That's why I supported the Stop Secret Spending Act, which requires this hidden spending to be reported on http://USAspending.gov like everything else. When Washington spends your money, you deserve to see the results.

Appreciate receiving the National Retail Federation’s “Hero of Main Street” award this week for my voting record in support of retailers and mom-and-pop shops across America. These folks keep our Main Streets thriving and our neighborhoods working; that’s why I’ve voted to curtail organized retail crime and ease the regulatory burden on our job creators.

The other side of the aisle tried to tank it with misleading attacks and scare tactics. I pray my colleagues do the right thing for the brave men and women who have served this country.

It directs the Pentagon to designate an executive agent to speed up joint R&D, identify Israeli-origin tech for integration into U.S. systems/programs of record, support co-production, data fusion/network integration, and industrial cooperation in areas like drones, AI, cyber, missiles, and quantum. It does **not** merge military commands, put U.S. forces under IDF control, or transfer decision-making authority to Israel. No joint operational structures or troop integration. This formalizes and deepens existing tech/industrial ties (common with close allies), but critics rightly note it creates deeper supply chain and tech entanglement that’s hard to unwind later. 🚨 The most important moment in the fight against cancer often comes before the diagnosis. It comes when a woman learns she is at greater risk. When she recognizes a warning sign. When her doctor knows what to look for. When a screening finds cancer early enough to change everything that follows. As Co-Chair of the House Cancer Caucus, expanding access to early detection, education, and risk-based care has been one of my highest priorities. Yesterday, the House delivered a major victory for women’s health and cancer prevention by passing my bipartisan EARLY Act reauthorization and including my bipartisan SCREENS for Cancer Act. Together, these bills protect those critical moments before a diagnosis—while helping more low-income, uninsured, and underserved women access lifesaving breast and cervical cancer screenings. My mother and sister are survivors. For our family, early detection is not an abstraction. It is how we know that the right information and the right care, delivered in time, can save a life. I urge my colleagues in the Senate to act without delay and send this lifesaving legislation to the President’s desk.

Historically, the NDAA has been a bipartisan bill that receives overwhelming support from Democrats and Republicans to provide our troops and their families with pay raises and critical funding for military construction projects, healthcare, and more. As the proud representative of Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, I understand why this funding is necessary and the impact it has on our military. Unfortunately, this NDAA includes unpopular, extremist policy riders. It also attaches the text of the SAVE America Act that would undermine the integrity of our elections and supercharge voter suppression. The SAVE America Act would create enormous barriers for servicemembers abroad to vote, and it would prevent millions of Americans from voting simply because they don’t have a passport. This deeply unpopular and unrelated bill should not be attached to the NDAA. One has nothing to do with the other. As a member of the House Appropriations Committee, I take federal spending seriously and believe that we must protect Congress’s power of the purse now more than ever. This NDAA authorizes an unprecedented $1.5 trillion to the Department of Defense while important health, housing, and food programs that millions rely on are being cut. This money would bolster the unauthorized and illegal war in Iran that has made life more expensive for every American. There is no justification for it and no clear strategy. This vote also comes on the heels of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth telling Congress he needs an extra $67 billion in additional funding to continue the war in Iran. I will continue fighting for a stronger bipartisan NDAA that addresses and funds the needs of our servicemembers and their families. I urge the Senate to remove the SAVE America Act and remedy the poison pills included in this bill as it has done in past years. I look forward to supporting a bipartisan final product after it has met those requirements.

📜STATEMENT: Rep. Roy Votes Against Bloated $1.15 Trillion NDAA. Rep. Roy: "While this year's National Defense Authorization Act takes some important steps toward restoring the Pentagon's focus on its core mission of defending the United States, there is still significant work to be done. I cannot support authorizing approximately $1.15 trillion in discretionary national defense spending—a staggering $251.1 billion, or 28%, increase over the previous year's authorization—without stronger accountability for how those taxpayer dollars will be spent. I was pleased that the House included several important conservative reforms in the final bill, including prohibiting taxpayer funding for transgender surgeries, making it easier for qualified servicemembers and Department of War personnel to carry firearms on military installations, and adopting my amendment to eliminate an unproven AI voice-analysis pilot that determines which servicemembers should face drug testing and potential discipline based on government behavioral surveillance. These are meaningful improvements that will better protect our servicemembers and refocus the military on its core mission. Unfortunately, those important reforms are outweighed by the bill's continued excessive spending and misplaced priorities, as the legislation continues to prioritize costly green energy initiatives by allowing the Department of War to purchase more expensive sustainable aviation fuel at taxpayer expense instead of focusing resources on military readiness and combat capability. The bill also falls short in promoting meaningful congressional accountability for ongoing military engagements by relying on a report on the costs of operations involving Iran rather than ensuring Congress fully debates the objectives, scope, and long-term fiscal implications of those operations. National security requires a strong military, but it also demands fiscal responsibility and disciplined oversight. Until Congress demonstrates the same commitment to reform and accountability that it does to increasing defense spending, I cannot support this legislation." https://roy.house.gov/media/press-releases/rep-roy-votes-against-bloated-115-trillion-ndaa

📜STATEMENT: Rep. Roy Votes for Stop Insider Trading Act, Continuing Longstanding Fight to Ban Congressional Stock Trading. Rep. Roy: "The American people deserve to know that their elected representatives are serving the public—not their own investment portfolios. Since my first term in Congress, I've fought to end congressional stock trading because public service should never be used for private gain. While I support the bill, I want to be clear that I believe this legislation should have been brought to the floor, amended, and voted on as a single subject matter—not combined with the voter ID portion of the SAVE America Act, of which I am the proud author.  To be clear, doing so was designed specifically to have most Democrats vote against it. I worked in good faith to ban congressional stock trading with colleagues on both sides of the aisle, and we should be voting on that work. I will continue to work to try to get that vote this Congress.   Nevertheless, today’s passage of the Stop Insider Trading Act is an important step toward restoring trust and ensuring that Members of Congress are held to the same standard of integrity the American people expect. I'm proud to have worked to advance this legislation with Chairman Steil and my colleagues Rep. Luna, Rep Burchett, Rep Fitzpatrick, among others, and will continue fighting for greater accountability to restore trust in Congress in Washington." https://roy.house.gov/media/press-releases/rep-roy-votes-stop-insider-trading-act-continuing-longstanding-fight-ban

📜STATEMENT: Rep. Roy Votes for Budget Resolution to Advance SAVE America Act Through Reconciliation. Rep. Roy: “While far from perfect, I voted in favor of this budget resolution because it is an important step in getting my SAVE America Act passed by the Senate. As the Senate takes up this legislation, there can be no compromise on election integrity. The full SAVE America Act must be included as a mandatory requirement for every state—not watered down into an optional policy incentivized through federal funding. Election security should not depend on whether states choose to participate, and my votes for future measures will fully depend on this. Just as importantly, Congress cannot continue adding to our fiscal crisis without accountability. I regret that this $90 billion budget resolution is not fully paid for. With our national debt approaching $40 trillion, the Senate should set its instructions to pay for it, and if not, the House leadership should commit now that any future funding legislation will fully offset the cost of this bill in real terms—dollar for dollar and year for year. Further, because much of the spending in this legislation is dedicated to providing our military with much-needed resources, we must take a firm position on the conflict with Iran. If we are to fund this effort, it must be backed by a clear mission and full commitment—not half-hearted acquiescence. I am swallowing this unpaid-for bill to try to pass election integrity and ensure our military heroes have the tools they need, but Washington's addiction to deficit spending and making war without full ownership must end for the benefit of our nation’s posterity." https://roy.house.gov/media/press-releases/rep-roy-votes-budget-resolution-advance-save-america-act-through

This year’s NDAA strengthens our national defense by rebuilding the defense industrial base, investing in next-generation technologies, improving military readiness, and providing our servicemembers with the resources and support they need. At a time when adversaries continue to challenge American interests, we must ensure our military has the tools, capabilities, and strategic advantage necessary to deter threats and protect our nation. B001317.text: Today, I voted “no” on the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for fiscal year 2027. While I support providing for a robust national defense, I could not in good conscience vote for this legislation as it authorizes a $263.4 billion (29.6%) increase over the authorized level for the previous fiscal year. Looking to history, we know that once a level of spending is authorized, appropriators will rarely provide less funding than the maximum allowed. Furthermore, departmental funding baselines almost never decrease over time. Our Founding Fathers believed that public debt was among “the greatest of the dangers to be feared.” As George Washington once wrote, “avoiding likewise the accumulation of debt, not only by shunning occasions of expense, but by vigorous exertions in time of peace to discharge the debts, which unavoidable wars may have occasioned, not ungenerously throwing upon posterity the burthen, which we ourselves ought to bear.” We are currently facing the largest national debt in our country’s history, owing over $39.5 trillion, and we simply cannot bear the cost of additional, unpaid-for spending. To achieve the transformative defense spending necessary for our nation’s future, we must either, in the current Reconciliation 3.0 or in a future reconciliation package, find meaningful offsets that would allow us to reach a higher annual defense spending target in a fiscally responsible way. Unlike providing additional defense funding in a reconciliation package, which is a one-time expenditure, this bill would be a $260 billion increase in the annual defense discretionary baseline that I could support if we offset the cost elsewhere. Without any further changes to spending, this would mean roughly $2.63 trillion in additional debt loading over the next ten years. While I cannot support this package due to my spending concerns, I support the SAVE America Act being joined to this legislation after final passage. I have voted in favor of the SAVE America Act and its predecessor, the SAVE Act, five times. I support leadership’s decision to join the SAVE America Act to other pieces of legislation whenever they can, but I cannot vote for legislation that could lead to an additional debt load of $2.63 trillion over the next ten years. I continue to be hopeful that we will be able to pass the SAVE America Act through the reconciliation process, which we advanced this week.

Thank you, Mr. President! As fiscal hawks in the House, we have put aside our spending offset demands in this measure SOLELY because of the expectation that this is the path for the Senate to pass the SAVE America Act in truth…not a ‘dead on arrival’ counterfeit version some in the Senate are advocating.
If Olive Garden can require photo ID for a Pasta Pass, surely America can require photo ID to vote! Pass the SAVE America Act immediately!!

J000311.text: Today, we mourn the passing of United States Senator Lindsey Graham, a fierce advocate for the people of South Carolina.  May his memory be a blessing to his family and friends. Born in Upstate South Carolina, tragedy struck Lindsey early in his life.  After he graduated from high school, Lindsey’s mother and father passed away within 15 months of each other, leaving him without parents and his 13-year-old sister orphaned.  Lindsey shifted his focus to raising and caring for his sister, assuming a responsibility few can imagine at that age. The resilience and sense of duty he developed during those difficult years would come to define a lifetime of service. For 33 years, Lindsey served our Country in the United States Air Force.  He was awarded the Bronze Star for meritorious service shortly before retiring as a Colonel. For 31 years, Lindsey served in the United States Congress, and became one of the most influential lawmakers in our Country. Lindsey’s unexpected passing also affirms a profound truth: every day we live is a gift and a blessing from God.

M001235.text: Press Release: Congressman Riley M. Moore Applauds House Passage of Reconciliation Budget Resolution and Stop Insider Trading Act Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Riley M. Moore joined his Republican colleagues in voting to pass the Budget Resolution for Reconciliation 3.0 - the SAVE and Protect America Act - and H.R. 7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act, two key measures advancing election integrity, government accountability, and President Trump’s America First agenda. The Budget Resolution for Reconciliation 3.0 paves the way for legislation to enact the SAVE America Act, strengthen America’s national defense, and protect the nation’s food supply. The Stop Insider Trading Act prohibits Members of Congress from purchasing individual stocks, helps prevent lawmakers from profiting from inside information, and includes a provision requiring federal voter ID at polling places. Congressman Riley M. Moore released the following statement: “Today, House Republicans delivered on two key priorities that the American people have been demanding: restoring trust in our government and securing our elections. By passing the Budget Resolution for Reconciliation 3.0, including the SAVE America Act, and the Stop Insider Trading Act, including a requirement to show an ID when voting in federal elections, we are sending a clear message: we will not tolerate election fraud or putting personal gain over public service anymore. I urge the Senate to pass these critical bills immediately.” The Budget Resolution now heads to the Senate, where passage will allow House committees to begin drafting the reconciliation legislation. The Stop Insider Trading Act also advances to the Senate for consideration.
